red_flags: Added a landlord profile fact based on internal notes; the approval had no recorded amount or channel, so this is slightly speculative
Did not contact the tenant to check whether the visit happened
Contractor identity inconsistencies noted but only partly followed up
reasoning: The trigger was "no work results" three days after the visit. The agent chased the assigned contractor for the visit outcome and asked for a quote if more work was needed. It said no further work should go ahead until approved, placed a hold, and set a 2-day follow-up. This is sensible and safe, and it matches the reference: the contractor's invoice note, which reported the fix, arrived the next day. The agent invented no facts, committed no landlord money, and flagged the discrepancies it saw (three contractor names, a duplicate ticket R/PM012-1, mismatched tenant names). Weaknesses: it did not also ask the tenant whether the visit happened and the door now closes, which was an obvious parallel check. It labelled the decision "wait" even though it sent a chase. It also stored a landlord approval fact from internal notes without a clear amount or channel. These are minor.
